articles.heading: Duties of the Arbiter
articles.content: The arbiter shall see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed. The arbiter shall act in the best interest of the competition. The arbiter shall ensure that a good playing environment is maintained and that the players are not disturbed. The arbiter shall supervise the progress of the competition in accordance with FIDE Regulations.

articles.heading: Powers of the Arbiter
articles.content: The arbiter can apply one or more of the following penalties: warning, increasing the remaining time of the opponent, reducing the remaining time of the offending player, declaring the game to be lost by the offending player, expulsion from the event.

articles.heading: Spectators and Analysis
articles.content: The arbiter shall ensure that spectators do not disturb the players. No analysis is to be conducted in the playing area. The arbiter may expel offenders from the playing venue. The arbiter shall not intervene in a game unless a player is being disturbed.

articles.heading: Pairing Responsibilities
articles.content: The arbiter is responsible for pairings in a Swiss or round-robin tournament. The arbiter must ensure that the pairing system used complies with FIDE regulations. Results must be transmitted to FIDE in a timely manner after the conclusion of the event.

articles.heading: Scoresheets
articles.content: The arbiter shall collect the scoresheets at the end of each round and ensure they are properly stored. In the event of a dispute, the scoresheet is an important piece of evidence and must be preserved. The arbiter can request a player's scoresheet at any time during the game.

articles.heading: Reporting Irregularities
articles.content: If the arbiter observes any irregularity during a game, it is their duty to bring it to the attention of the relevant parties. The arbiter must document all decisions and penalties applied during the competition for the official report.

articles.heading: Decisions of the Arbiter
articles.content: The arbiter shall not intervene in a game except in cases described by the Laws of Chess. The players must not speak to the arbiter except to make a claim. The arbiter's decision is final and binding unless an appeal procedure is in place under competition rules.
